A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same context-length scaling framework. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLaMa measurements, GPT-2 training experiments on OpenWebText, and synthetic parity experiments, including additional entropy analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 reports original language-model and synthetic-data experiments, including revised OpenWebText results, Transformer-based parity experiments, and Gaussian-KDE entropy measurements.

M1.justification: The auxiliary synthetic model is substantially redesigned: v1 Appendix C.4 uses a masked-context MLP with a separate task embedding, whereas v3 Appendix B.6 uses a causal Transformer with RoPE and a single task token. This changes architecture and input processing. The main Section 4 MLP models remain.

E1.justification: Both versions cover OpenWebText, the separately collected filtered-word corpus, and position-weighted sparse-parity tasks. Unequal task frequencies already appear in v1 Appendix C.4. Larger training budgets and different models in v3 change settings within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 9 adds Gaussian-KDE as an evaluated alternative to PCA-based entropy estimation and directly compares their estimates. The calculated Bayes-loss and random-guess reference comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix F.1.1 changes reported OpenWebText training sizes from 12/25/50M to 200–750M tokens, reduces warm-up from 2000 to 1000 iterations, and replaces validation-based checkpoint selection with matched iteration counts across context lengths for each token budget. v3 also revises synthetic masking settings and adds a KDE measurement protocol. Section 3 retains conflicting stopping-language, but the reported protocol revision is explicit.

E4.justification: v3 Appendix B.3.2 adds an estimator-robustness check testing whether entropy relationships persist with Gaussian-KDE. Its revised synthetic analysis in Figure 11 adds correlations between CE loss and PCA-derived intrinsic dimension across thresholds, alongside entropy correlations already examined in v1 Figure 13.

E5.justification: Both versions report fitted-parameter ± quantities in Section 4.3 and correlation or fit summaries elsewhere. No change to explicit seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practices is documented.

E6.justification: OpenWebText loss curves are replaced under revised budgets and settings. Table 1 replaces MLP results with Transformer results, including 0.478 versus 0.4648 model loss at context length 17, and removes the length-15 and length-60 rows; these are not same-setting gains. Section 4.3 changes several fitted-coefficient signs, and Figure 9 adds KDE correlation results.

T1.justification: v3 adds the conditional CE/KL derivation in Appendix A.2, formal intrinsic-space and decoder definitions, density regularity assumptions, and nearest-neighbor and approximation-loss theorems with proofs in Appendix C.1–C.2. It also revises the entropy premise using predictive information gain. The earlier s-bits Bayes-risk argument is retained within C.3.

C1.justification: The abstract's main framework, empirical-validation contributions, and optimal-context-length claim remain. v3 additionally emphasizes formal definitions and theorem derivations in the introduction and conclusion, and removes the conclusion's explicit training-until-overfitting qualification from the optimal-length claim.

C2.justification: v3 Section 5.2 newly qualifies intrinsic space as dependent on the model and prediction task, distinguishing this explanation from possible model-agnostic accounts. It removes v1's concluding speculation that finite intrinsic dimension could explain successful language modeling with finite-state RNNs. The limitation concerning staged long-context training remains.

D1.justification: Technical reporting is substantially revised for the changed experiments. v3 specifies Transformer dimensions, RoPE settings, token inputs, and KDE sample count and bandwidth. Appendix F revises training instructions and resource accounting while omitting v1's effective batch size, learning-rate decay schedule, and checkpoint-selection details. The experiment-code access link is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Barak et al.'s parity study and Chen et al.'s L2M, explaining complementary dataset-limited and hidden-state-limited bounds in Appendix G.4. It also explicitly positions its new scaling derivation as requiring weaker assumptions than Bahri et al. Most earlier related-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: The preliminaries are reorganized into three subsections, the entropy exposition is substantially expanded and subdivided, and related work moves from Section 5 to Appendix G. Earlier derivations are integrated into the reorganized appendices. Prose, terminology, and the author/affiliation block are edited throughout.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. v1 Figures 3–4 are merged into v3 Figure 3, Figures 6–7 into Figure 4, and Figure 1's panels become side by side. The raw OpenWebText plot moves to the appendix; synthetic diagrams and plots are replaced, and KDE plots and an assumption/theorem summary table are added.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v3 adds useful KDE corroboration, a synthetic model closer to calculated Bayes loss, and more explicit theoretical assumptions. However, the new Theorem 2 states an unaveraged bound in Equation 28 while its proof establishes only an expected bound in Equation 30. Section 3's stopping description also conflicts with revised Appendix F.1.1. These problems affect the new theoretical and empirical support, leaving the net quality improvement uncertain.
